title: At the Market
author: Léxi
desc: Acheter, demander un prix et négocier en anglais.

p: Kofi is in Accra, in Ghana, for the first time. In Ghana, people speak English. He goes to Makola market.
"Good morning, sister!" says a seller with a big smile.
"Good morning! How are you?"
"I'm fine, thank you. And you? What do you want today?"
"I want some pineapples, please. How much is one pineapple?"
"One pineapple is ten cedis."
"Ten cedis? That's expensive!"
"It's a very sweet pineapple, my brother. Taste it!"
She gives him a small piece. Kofi tastes it. "Mmm. It's very sweet!"
"OK, I want three pineapples. Can you give me a good price?"
"Three pineapples is thirty cedis. For you, twenty-eight."
"Twenty-five, please. I'm a student."
The seller laughs. "Everybody is a student today! OK, OK. Twenty-six, and I give you a mango."
"Deal!" says Kofi. "Thank you very much."
He gives her thirty cedis. "Here you are."
"Here is your change: four cedis. And your mango. Come back tomorrow!"
"See you tomorrow! Have a nice day!"
Here are the sentences Kofi used. You can use them in any market, in any English-speaking country:

*How much is this?* — C'est combien ?
*That's too expensive.* — C'est trop cher.
*Can you give me a good price?* — Tu peux me faire un bon prix ?
*I'll take it.* — Je le prends.
*Do you have change?* — Tu as la monnaie ?
*Can I have a bag, please?* — Je peux avoir un sachet, s'il te plaît ?
Now practise! Read the dialogue again, out loud, with a friend. One person is Kofi, the other is the seller.
